description: The evolutionary programmer builds a path planner by evolution instead of by hand. A genome is a short bit string (18 bits here) that encodes a whole genetic algorithm for path planning: its selection operator and parameter, elitism, crossover and mutation rates, population size, the size of the detour search, and a generational or steady-state scheme. To score a genome, the method decodes it, runs that planner on a set of training graphs with a fixed evaluation budget and fixed seeds, and takes the mean excess of the found path length over the shortest length from Dijkstra's algorithm. A *meta-GA* with linear-ranking selection then evolves these bit strings. Use it to tune a planner for a family of maps; the result is the best configuration found for the training maps, not a guarantee for new ones.

papers.authors: Jiabin Lou, Rong Ding, Wenjun Wu
papers.title: Evolutionary Programmer: Autonomously Creating Path Planning Programs based on Evolutionary Algorithms
